explanation: The thumbs-up is a well-established positive gesture in India, roughly equivalent to the Western 'okay' or 'good job' sign — it even features on India's one-rupee coin and gave its name to the popular Thums Up cola brand. It is used casually across ages and most everyday contexts without being seen as rude, unlike in a handful of other countries where the same gesture is an insult.
local_tip: A thumbs-up to show approval or agreement reads as positive in India in both casual and most everyday situations.

also_check.note: The thumbs-up is an insult in Iran, roughly equivalent to an obscene gesture.
Considered offensive in Afghanistan, similar to its negative meaning in Iran and parts of the Middle East.
